'''''Eriocapitella japonica''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the buttercup family [[Ranunculaceae]] commonly cultivated as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental]]. The [[specific epithet]] ''japonica'' means "from Japan",{{sfnp|Gledhill|2008|p=220}} which is a misnomer since the species is introduced in [[Japan]]. It is [[Native plant|native]] to [[China]], [[Taiwan]], and [[Vietnam]].{{r|POWO}}  It was formerly a member of genus ''[[Anemone]]'' and shares the common name '''[[Japanese anemone (disambiguation)|Japanese anemone]]''' with several other ''Eriocapitella'' species.<ref>{{cite book |title=Encyclopaedia of Border Plants |first=Hanneke |last=van Dijk |entry=Anemone |entry-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Dp3lsHz1d2oC&newbks=1&newbks_redir=0&printsec=frontcover#v=onepage&q&f=false |publisher=Rebo |date=1997 |page=41 |ISBN=9781579582029 |quote=There are four species of Japanese anemone: ''Anemone hupehensis'', ''Anemone × hybrida'', ''Anemone vitifolia'' and ''Anemone tomentosa''.}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS: Introducing... Japanese anemones|url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/anemone/japanese | access-date = 5 September 2025}}</ref>

==Description==

''Eriocapitella japonica'' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[herbaceous plant]] that stands {{cvt|60|to|90|cm|ft|0}} high. Plant parts are soft and downy, with short hairs. The [[basal leaf|basal leaves]] are [[Glossary_of_leaf_morphology#Leaf_structure|ternate]], lobed, and toothed. The [[inflorescence]] is a [[Inflorescence#Determinate_or_cymose|cyme]] with flower stalks rising from a [[Whorl (botany)|whorl]] of leaves wrapped around the top of the stem. Each [[flower]] is approximately {{cvt|5|to|7.5|cm|in|1}} across, with 1–3 whorls of [[sepal]]s (but no [[petal]]s) and yellow [[stamen]]s. The sepals are rosy purple or [[Carmine_(color)|carmine]] in color. The [[fruit]]s are silky [[achene]]s.{{r|Bailey1919}}

==Taxonomy==

''Eriocapitella japonica'' was described by [[Takenoshin Nakai]] in 1941.{{r|IPNI}} Like other members of genus ''[[Eriocapitella]]'', ''E. japonica'' was formerly a member of genus ''[[Anemone]]''. The historically important synonym ''Anemone hupehensis'' var. ''japonica'' <small>(Thunb.) Bowles & Stearn</small> was described in 1947.{{r|POWO:77083631-1}}

''E. japonica'' has the longest taxonomic history of any member of genus ''Eriocapitella''. The [[basionym]] ''Atragene japonica'' <small>Thunb.</small> was described by [[Carl Peter Thunberg|Carl Thunberg]] in 1784.{{r|POWO:927386-1}} Thunberg, one of the [[Apostles of Linnaeus]], had collected dried specimens while working as a doctor for the [[Dutch East Indies Company]].{{r|Klingaman2006}}

''E. japonica'' was previously known as ''Anemone japonica'' <small>(Thunb.) Siebold & Zucc.</small> The latter had at least three named varieties: ''A. j.'' var. ''hupehensis'', ''A. j.'' var. ''hybrida'', and ''A. j.'' var. ''tomentosa'',{{r|IPNI:search}} now known as [[Eriocapitella hupehensis|''E. hupehensis'']], [[Eriocapitella × hybrida|''E.'' × ''hybrida'']], and [[Eriocapitella tomentosa|''E. tomentosa'']], respectively. Along with [[Eriocapitella vitifolia|''E. vitifolia'']], ''E. japonica'' is a parent of the hybrid ''E.'' × ''hybrida''.{{sfnp|Rudy|2004|p=1}}

==Distribution==

''Eriocapitella japonica'' is [[Native plant|native]] to [[Central China]], [[East China]], [[South China]], [[Taiwan]], and [[Vietnam]].{{r|POWO}} It has been cultivated and [[Naturalization|naturalized]] in the following Chinese provinces:{{r|FOC}}

* East China: [[Anhui]], [[Jiangsu]], Jiangxi, Zhejiang, [[Fujian]]
* South China: [[Guangdong]]
* Southwest China: [[Yunnan]]

''E. japonica'' was introduced to [[Japan]] and [[Korea]].{{r|POWO}} It has been naturalized in Japan for hundreds of years.{{sfnp|Herman|2004}}

==Ecology==

''Eriocapitella japonica'' along with four other [[taxa]] ([[Eriocapitella hupehensis|''E. hupehensis'']], ''E. vitifolia'', [[Eriocapitella tomentosa|''E. tomentosa'']], and ''E.'' × ''hybrida'') are known as '''fall-blooming anemones'''.{{sfnp|Rudy|2004}} Like ''E. hupehensis'', ''E. japonica'' flowers from July to October in its native habitat.{{r|FOC}}

==Cultivation==

Varieties of ''Eriocapitella japonica'' are cultivated worldwide, especially in [[China]], [[Japan]], and [[Korea]], where naturalized populations are known to exist. Hundreds of years ago, a form of [[Eriocapitella hupehensis|''E. hupehensis'']] with smaller, semi-double flowers and pink sepals escaped cultivation and spread across China to Japan and Korea. After finding this form in a Shanghai graveyard in 1843, the plant explorer [[Robert Fortune]] sent it home to England where it became known as ''E. japonica'', the '''Japanese anemone'''. European [[Horticulture |horticulturists]] crossed the Japanese anemone with [[Eriocapitella vitifolia|''E. vitifolia'']] to produce [[cultivar]]s of the artificial hybrid [[Eriocapitella × hybrida|''E.'' × ''hybrida'']].{{sfnp|Herman|2004}}

At the [[Chicago Botanic Garden]], Rudy experimented with 26 cultivars of fall-blooming anemones over a 5-year period beginning in 1998. His experiments included 4 cultivars of ''E. japonica'', one of which (''E. japonica'' 'Prinz Heinrich') had the longest bloom length (65 days) of any cultivar.{{sfnp|Rudy|2004}}

{{As of|March 2020}}, the following cultivars have gained the [[Award of Garden Merit]] (AGM) from the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]:{{r|AGM}}

* ''E. japonica'' 'Pamina'
* ''E. japonica'' 'Rotkäppchen'{{r|RHS:Rotkappchen}}

The cultivar ''E. japonica'' 'Prinz Heinrich' was removed from the AGM list in 2013.
